specific_attraction: Lands End trail + Sutro Baths ruins, Bernal Heights summit at sunset, Mission murals (Balmy Alley, Clarion Alley)
why_worth_it: The Lands End coastal trail with the ruined Sutro Baths pool is the SF viewpoint most visitors skip for Golden Gate Bridge photos, and it is better.
food_drink_pick: Mission burrito at La Taqueria; Tartine Bakery morning bun
best_time: Year round; clearest skies Sep to Oct

specific_attraction: Ferry Building marketplace, Presidio Tunnel Tops, Golden Gate Bridge walk at Fort Point (not the overlook lot everyone drives to)
why_worth_it: Fort Point puts you directly under the bridge deck looking up, a completely different photo and far less crowded than the vista point.
food_drink_pick: Ferry Building: Cowgirl Creamery, Hog Island oysters
best_time: Year round

specific_attraction: Healdsburg plaza, a small family Sonoma winery instead of a Napa bus tour, Armstrong Redwoods
why_worth_it: Healdsburg is the local answer to Napa crowding, a walkable plaza ringed by tasting rooms instead of a highway strip.
food_drink_pick: Shed Healdsburg for lunch
best_time: Apr to Oct for harvest energy; year round for tasting

specific_attraction: Emerald Bay overlook, Sand Harbor on the Nevada side at sunrise, a lake ferry or kayak on the clearest water in the state
why_worth_it: Sand Harbor at sunrise before the parking lot fills is the single best water clarity shot in the Sierra.
food_drink_pick: South Lake brewery after a day on the water
best_time: Jun to Sep for swimming and hiking; Dec to Mar for skiing, roads can need chains

specific_attraction: Tunnel View at golden hour, Mist Trail to Vernal Fall, Glacier Point at night for stars
why_worth_it: Tioga Pass across the high country only opens roughly late May to Oct, and it is the scenic way in rather than backtracking through the valley entrance twice.
food_drink_pick: Picnic from the Village Store, avoid the lodge restaurant lines
best_time: May to Oct for Tioga Pass access; year round via Highway 140, waterfalls peak Apr to Jun

specific_attraction: General Sherman Tree, Moro Rock climb, Crystal Cave (reserve ahead)
why_worth_it: The largest tree on earth by volume gets a fraction of Yosemite's crowds because it is a longer drive from anywhere.
best_time: May to Oct, snow can close the high sections in winter

specific_attraction: Bishop Peak sunrise hike, Bubblegum Alley, a cheap SLO farmers market Thursday night
why_worth_it: Thursday night farmers market on Higuera closes the street for barbecue smoke and live music, a genuinely local Central Coast night.
food_drink_pick: Tri-tip sandwich from the farmers market grills
best_time: Thursday nights year round

specific_attraction: McWay Falls overlook, Bixby Bridge at sunrise before the tour buses, Pfeiffer Beach purple sand (unmarked turnoff)
why_worth_it: Pfeiffer Beach has no sign from Highway 1 on purpose; the purple sand and keyhole rock make it worth finding.
food_drink_pick: Nepenthe restaurant view, or a cheaper picnic below it
best_time: Apr to Jun and Sep to Nov for clearest coastal weather

specific_attraction: Griffith Observatory at sunset, Hollywood sign from the Hollyridge Trail (not the tourist overlook parking), Grand Central Market lunch
why_worth_it: Hiking to the sign gets you the actual summit view for free instead of paying for a distant overlook photo.
food_drink_pick: Grand Central Market: Eggslut or Villa Moreliana
best_time: Year round, clearest skies after a winter rain

specific_attraction: The Getty Center (free, book timed parking), Venice canals and boardwalk, Abbot Kinney
why_worth_it: Free admission and one of the best art collections on the West Coast, most first time visitors skip it entirely.
food_drink_pick: Gjelina on Abbot Kinney
best_time: Year round

specific_attraction: Sunset Cliffs, Balboa Park museums, La Jolla Cove seals and snorkeling
why_worth_it: Sunset Cliffs is a free, uncrowded alternative to La Jolla for the same golden hour ocean drama.
food_drink_pick: Fish tacos in Ocean Beach
best_time: Year round, La Jolla seal pupping season Jan to Jun

specific_attraction: Palm Springs Aerial Tramway, Joshua Tree at sunrise, mid century modern architecture tour
why_worth_it: The tramway climbs from desert floor to alpine forest in under 10 minutes, the fastest ecosystem change you can drive to in SoCal.
food_drink_pick: Date shake at Shields in Indio
best_time: Oct to Apr, summer desert heat is genuinely dangerous

specific_attraction: Santa Barbara Courthouse sunset tower view (free), State Street, Butterfly Beach
why_worth_it: The courthouse clock tower is a free unmarked viewpoint most day trippers never learn about.
best_time: Year round

section: OC weekend getaways / hangouts (in and out of OC)
specific_attraction: Heisler Park tide pools at low tide, Thousand Steps Beach, gallery walk on First Thursdays
why_worth_it: Tide pools at Heisler are the best easy access marine life in OC, check a tide chart first.
food_drink_pick: The Stand for a smoothie
best_time: Check tide chart; lowest tides best, any season

section: OC weekend getaways / hangouts (in and out of OC)
specific_attraction: Whale watching charter (grey whales winter, blue whales summer), Dana Point Harbor, Salt Creek Beach
why_worth_it: OC sits on one of the best whale migration corridors in the country and most locals never book the boat.
food_drink_pick: Harbor seafood shack
best_time: Dec to Mar grey whales, Jun to Sep blue whales

section: OC weekend getaways / hangouts (in and out of OC)
specific_attraction: Bolsa Avenue food crawl, Asian Garden Mall, a proper banh mi and che dessert stop
why_worth_it: The largest Vietnamese community outside Vietnam, worth treating as a real food destination rather than a drive through.
food_drink_pick: Banh mi at a Bolsa Ave bakery; che at a dessert shop
best_time: Year round

section: OC weekend getaways / hangouts (in and out of OC)
specific_attraction: Huntington Beach Pier sunset, surf lesson, Pacific Airshow if the dates line up
why_worth_it: Surf City USA, a genuinely good beginner surf beach if you have never tried.
food_drink_pick: Ruby's Diner on the pier
best_time: Pacific Airshow is usually October, VERIFY dates

section: OC weekend getaways / hangouts (in and out of OC)

specific_attraction: Glass bottom boat, golf cart rental around Avalon, zip line eco tour
why_worth_it: A genuine island getaway that is a same day round trip from OC, no passport needed.
food_drink_pick: Avalon seafood on the harbor

section: OC weekend getaways / hangouts (in and out of OC)
specific_attraction: Lake Big Bear kayaking or skiing depending on season, Alpine Slide, a cabin weekend
why_worth_it: The closest snow to Orange County, roughly a two hour drive for a genuine mountain weekend.
food_drink_pick: Cabin cooked meals cheaper than the lodges
best_time: Dec to Mar skiing, Jun to Sep lake activities

section: OC weekend getaways / hangouts (in and out of OC)
specific_attraction: Hot air balloon ride over the vineyards at sunrise, wine tasting flight, Old Town Temecula
why_worth_it: A closer, cheaper Wine Country than Napa for a one day OC escape.
food_drink_pick: Wine tasting flight at a family winery
best_time: Aug to Oct for harvest, calm mornings best for ballooning year round

section: OC weekend getaways / hangouts (in and out of OC)
specific_attraction: The Strip at night, a residency show, Red Rock Canyon day trip
why_worth_it: Close enough for a genuine weekend, far enough to feel like a different trip entirely.
food_drink_pick: Buffet or a strip food hall
best_time: Spring and fall for milder desert heat

section: Channel Islands National Park, Catalina Island, and Coronado.
specific_attraction: Santa Cruz Island sea caves by kayak, Anacapa Island arch, Santa Rosa Island backcountry camping
why_worth_it: California's least visited national park, five islands with wildlife found nowhere else on earth including the island fox.
food_drink_pick: Pack your own, no services on most islands
best_time: Apr to Oct for calmer crossings, whale season Dec to Apr for the boat ride

section: Channel Islands National Park, Catalina Island, and Coronado.
specific_attraction: See Cali OC Weekend section for the standard visit; here as an overnight island stay with a hike to the interior
why_worth_it: Two Harbors on the far side of the island is the quiet, undeveloped Catalina almost no day tripper reaches.
best_time: Apr to Oct

section: Channel Islands National Park, Catalina Island, and Coronado.
transport: Ferry or drive over the bridge
specific_attraction: Hotel del Coronado, Coronado Beach, technically a peninsula rather than a true island but grouped here for the trip
why_worth_it: The sand here has a natural mica sparkle visible up close, a small detail almost nobody stops to notice.
food_drink_pick: Hotel Del afternoon tea
best_time: Year round

section: Whole California + neighboring states / Mexico border area
specific_attraction: Extend the NorCal loop into Nevada: Reno for one night, Virginia City ghost town
why_worth_it: A genuine Old West silver mining town a short detour from the Tahoe leg of a California loop.
best_time: Year round

section: Whole California + neighboring states / Mexico border area
specific_attraction: South Rim sunrise at Mather Point, a short hike below the rim on Bright Angel Trail
why_worth_it: If a California loop already reaches Las Vegas, the Grand Canyon is close enough to fold in rather than treat as a separate trip.
food_drink_pick: Pack a lunch, services inside the park are limited and pricey
best_time: Apr to May and Sep to Oct for mild rim weather

section: Whole California + neighboring states / Mexico border area
specific_attraction: Rim Drive loop, the deepest lake in the US, bluest water you will see on the whole trip
why_worth_it: Extending a NorCal trip north into Oregon reaches a genuinely different landscape within one long driving day.
best_time: Jul to Sep, the full Rim Drive is snowed shut most other months

section: Whole California + neighboring states / Mexico border area
specific_attraction: Valle de Guadalupe wine tasting (Mexico's answer to Napa), fish tacos at Mercado Negro, La Bufadora blowhole
why_worth_it: A real wine region a two hour drive south of San Diego, with a fraction of the Napa crowds and prices.
food_drink_pick: Fish tacos at Mercado Negro, Ensenada
best_time: Passport required for the return crossing; Aug to Oct for harvest, border wait times VERIFY before you go

section: Whole California + neighboring states / Mexico border area
transport: Walk across the San Ysidro border crossing
specific_attraction: Avenida Revolucion food and craft scene, Telefonica Gastro Park food trucks, Caesar salad origin story at Caesar's restaurant
why_worth_it: A walkable border city day trip; leaving the car at a San Ysidro lot and walking across avoids Mexican car insurance entirely.
food_drink_pick: Original Caesar salad at Caesar's
best_time: Check current border wait times and travel advisories before crossing

city_region: Baja Coast (Rosarito, Ensenada, Valle de Guadalupe)
overnight: Ensenada or a Valle de Guadalupe inn
route: OC → cross the San Ysidro or Otay Mesa border
specific_attraction: Rosarito beach and street tacos on day 1, Ensenada seafood market and La Bufadora, Valle de Guadalupe wine tasting on the way back
why_worth_it: The one truly nearby international getaway, three towns on one corridor instead of three separate trips.
food_drink_pick: Fish tacos at Mercado Negro, a Valle de Guadalupe tasting flight
best_time: Passport required for the return crossing; VERIFY current border wait times and whether an FMM tourist permit is needed past the free zone before you go

city_region: Los Cabos (Cabo San Lucas + San José del Cabo)
specific_attraction: El Arco boat trip, Medano Beach, San José del Cabo Art Walk on Thursdays
why_worth_it: The shortest international flight on this list, resort infrastructure built specifically for exactly this length of trip.
food_drink_pick: Fresh ceviche on the marina
best_time: Nov to Apr for milder heat and lower hurricane risk

specific_attraction: Malecón boardwalk, a jungle zipline canopy tour, the Boca de Tomatlán to Las Ánimas coastal hike
why_worth_it: Jungle and ocean in the same afternoon, a genuinely different landscape from the desert/beach options closer to home.
food_drink_pick: Fish tacos, birria
best_time: Nov to Apr for driest weather

city_region: Vancouver, BC (Victoria as an add-on, not a separate trip)
specific_attraction: Stanley Park seawall, Granville Island Market, Capilano Suspension Bridge; a ferry day trip to Victoria and Butchart Gardens if staying the full 3 days
why_worth_it: A genuinely different, mountain-ringed international city a 3 hour direct flight away.
food_drink_pick: Granville Island food stalls
best_time: May to Sep for driest weather; passport required

route: SNA/LAX → MEX (red eye recommended both ways)
specific_attraction: Teotihuacan pyramids, Frida Kahlo's Casa Azul, a Roma Norte taco crawl
why_worth_it: One of the great food cities in the world, though this is the most aggressive flight time on the list for only 3 days.
time_needed: 3 days (tight; a 4th day helps a lot)
food_drink_pick: Tacos al pastor, mezcal in Roma Norte
best_time: Mar to May and Sep to Nov for mild weather; book a red eye flight both ways to protect ground time

city_region: La Paz + Todos Santos, Baja Sur
specific_attraction: Whale shark swimming in La Paz bay (seasonal), Todos Santos art town, a boat trip to Isla Espíritu Santo
why_worth_it: A quieter, less resort-built alternative to Los Cabos with genuinely wild marine life close to shore.
food_drink_pick: Fresh oysters on the malecón
best_time: Oct to Apr for whale sharks

specific_attraction: Sea of Cortez island boat trips, 17th century mission town, Sierra de la Giganta canyon hikes
why_worth_it: The quietest, least developed option on this list, worth it specifically because almost nobody else is there.
best_time: Oct to May for milder heat

section: Red rock, canyon and dune country reachable by drive or a short flight.
specific_attraction: Cathedral Rock and Bell Rock vortex trails, Chapel of the Holy Cross, stargazing away from the resort lights
why_worth_it: Red rock formations and legitimately dark night skies, and it pairs naturally with the Grand Canyon if you have a 3rd day.
best_time: Mar to May and Sep to Nov for mild hiking temperatures

section: Red rock, canyon and dune country reachable by drive or a short flight.
city_region: Grand Canyon South Rim (pair with Sedona or Vegas, not standalone)
specific_attraction: Sunrise at Mather Point, a short hike below the rim on Bright Angel Trail
why_worth_it: On its own it is a lot of driving for one viewpoint-heavy day; tacked onto a Sedona or Las Vegas trip it earns its place.
time_needed: 1 to 1.5 days added to another trip
food_drink_pick: Pack a lunch, services inside the park are limited and pricey
best_time: Apr to May and Sep to Oct for mild rim weather

section: Red rock, canyon and dune country reachable by drive or a short flight.
specific_attraction: The Narrows river hike, Angels Landing (permit lottery — VERIFY current system), Emerald Pools
why_worth_it: Sheer sandstone cliffs and a hike that goes through a river inside a canyon, genuinely unlike anywhere in California.
time_needed: 3 days (2 is tight given the drive)
best_time: Apr to May and Sep to Oct; Angels Landing now requires a permit, VERIFY the current lottery system before you go

section: Red rock, canyon and dune country reachable by drive or a short flight.
specific_attraction: Badwater Basin (lowest point in North America), Zabriskie Point at sunrise, Mesquite Flat sand dunes
why_worth_it: The most otherworldly landscape reachable in a single day's drive from Orange County.
best_time: Nov to Mar only — summer ground temperatures are genuinely dangerous, this is not a summer trip

section: Red rock, canyon and dune country reachable by drive or a short flight.
city_region: Las Vegas + Valley of Fire State Park
specific_attraction: The Strip at night, a residency show, Valley of Fire's red sandstone as a 1 hour side trip, Red Rock Canyon
why_worth_it: Close enough for a genuine weekend, and Valley of Fire turns one afternoon into real desert scenery without a separate trip.
food_drink_pick: Buffet or a strip food hall
best_time: Spring and fall for milder desert heat

section: Red rock, canyon and dune country reachable by drive or a short flight.
transport: Drive (or fly to Grand Junction/SLC + drive)
specific_attraction: Delicate Arch at sunset, Canyonlands Island in the Sky overlook
why_worth_it: The single best sandstone arch scenery in the country, but honestly a long way to drive for 2 days — treat 3 days as the minimum.
best_time: Apr to May and Sep to Oct, summer heat is severe

specific_attraction: Orca and whale watching by boat, biking Friday Harbor, Lime Kiln Point sunset
why_worth_it: The best whale watching odds in the continental US, and it slots naturally onto the end of a Seattle trip.
time_needed: 1 to 2 days added to a Seattle trip
best_time: May to Sep for the best whale sighting odds

city_region: Oahu, Maui or Kauai (needs a long weekend, not a strict 3 day)
specific_attraction: Oahu: Diamond Head + North Shore. Maui: Road to Hana. Kauai: Nā Pali Coast.
why_worth_it: Genuinely worth it, but budget a Thursday to Sunday trip rather than Friday to Sunday, the flight alone is 11 to 12 hours round trip.
time_needed: 4 days recommended, 3 is possible but tight
food_drink_pick: Poke, shave ice
best_time: Apr to Jun and Sep to Nov for good weather and lower prices

city_region: Vancouver Island (pair with Vancouver, not standalone)
route: Vancouver → ferry or seaplane to Victoria
specific_attraction: Butchart Gardens, Inner Harbour high tea, whale watching in the Juan de Fuca Strait
why_worth_it: A genuinely different, more English feeling city, best added as a day or two onto a Vancouver trip rather than flown to on its own.
time_needed: 1 to 2 days added to a Vancouver trip
food_drink_pick: Afternoon tea at the Fairmont Empress
best_time: May to Sep for whale watching and garden blooms

specific_attraction: Convict Lake and Lake Mary hikes, Devils Postpile, skiing or snowboarding in season
why_worth_it: The fastest way to go from Orange County warmth to genuine alpine scenery.
best_time: Dec to Mar skiing, Jun to Sep hiking

specific_attraction: Historic Main Street, skiing at Park City Mountain or Deer Valley, a Utah Olympic Park tour
why_worth_it: The most convenient real ski town reachable by direct flight from SoCal.
best_time: Dec to Mar for skiing, Jun to Sep for hiking and mountain biking

route: SNA/LAX → ASE (seasonal direct) or DEN + drive
specific_attraction: Maroon Bells (one of the most photographed mountain views in the US), downtown gallery walk, skiing in season
why_worth_it: The most striking single mountain view on this list, though it is also the most expensive.
best_time: Direct SNA/LAX to Aspen flights are typically winter ski season only, VERIFY current routes; Jun to Sep for Maroon Bells without snow

specific_attraction: Suicide Rock and Devils Slide trail hikes, the Idyllwild Nature Center, a quiet artsy mountain town
why_worth_it: The closest genuine mountain-town escape to Orange County, easily doable as a single overnight.
food_drink_pick: Idyllwild fudge and pie shops
best_time: Year round; Jun to Oct for the clearest trail conditions, winter can bring snow

why_worth_it: A genuinely different, more laid back coastal college town than anything in SoCal.

section: Major & Distinct Cities (new NorCal/Central Coast stops, plus out of state)
specific_attraction: Downtown square wine tasting rooms, Lake Nacimiento watersports, rolling oak-covered back roads
why_worth_it: A closer, more relaxed wine region than Napa for a genuine 2 day trip.

best_time: Aug to Oct for harvest, spring for wildflowers

section: Major & Distinct Cities (new NorCal/Central Coast stops, plus out of state)

why_worth_it: A genuinely strange, opulent castle tour plus a beach that has wild elephant seals hauled out on it most of the year.

specific_attraction: San Jose, CA

best_time: FACT

why_worth_it: A genuinely different climate and culture, and Mount Rainier is close enough to add as a full day.

section: Major & Distinct Cities (new NorCal/Central Coast stops, plus out of state)
specific_attraction: Food cart pods, Powell's City of Books, Multnomah Falls in the Columbia River Gorge
why_worth_it: One of the best food scenes in the country for the price, plus a genuine waterfall day trip.

why_worth_it: Mile-high city with genuine mountain scenery 30 minutes outside downtown.
food_drink_pick: A RiNo brewery crawl
best_time: May to Sep for hiking, Sep to Mar for skiing side trips

section: Major & Distinct Cities (new NorCal/Central Coast stops, plus out of state)
specific_attraction: South Congress live music, historic barbecue, Barton Springs swim, paddleboarding Lady Bird Lake
why_worth_it: The best live music and barbecue combination reachable by direct flight.

why_worth_it: A completely different climate and skyline, and the architecture river cruise is genuinely worth the money.
food_drink_pick: Deep dish, an Italian beef sandwich

section: Major & Distinct Cities (new NorCal/Central Coast stops, plus out of state)
specific_attraction: French Quarter jazz clubs, Garden District architecture walk, an airboat swamp tour
why_worth_it: Music, food and architecture in one place, unlike anywhere else on this list.
food_drink_pick: Beignets, gumbo, a po'boy

section: Major & Distinct Cities (new NorCal/Central Coast stops, plus out of state)
specific_attraction: Broadway honky-tonk crawl, Ryman Auditorium tour, hot chicken
why_worth_it: Live music density is higher here than almost anywhere else in the country.

best_time: Apr to Jun and Sep to Oct

section: Major & Distinct Cities (new NorCal/Central Coast stops, plus out of state)
specific_attraction: Temple Square, Wasatch Mountains day hike (Lake Blanche Trail), craft breweries
why_worth_it: The shortest flight to real alpine hiking on this whole list.
best_time: Jun to Sep for hiking, Dec to Mar for skiing side trips

section: Major & Distinct Cities (new NorCal/Central Coast stops, plus out of state)
specific_attraction: The River Walk, the Alamo, biking the 15 mile Mission Trail, Natural Bridge Caverns
why_worth_it: More historically layered than most Texas cities, and genuinely walkable.
food_drink_pick: Tex-Mex on the River Walk
best_time: Mar to May and Oct to Nov

section: Major & Distinct Cities (new NorCal/Central Coast stops, plus out of state)
route: OC → ABQ + drive or direct seasonal
specific_attraction: Historic Plaza, Pueblo-style adobe architecture, Georgia O'Keeffe Museum, high desert art galleries
why_worth_it: A completely different, older architectural tradition than anywhere else in the Southwest on this list.
food_drink_pick: Green chile on everything
best_time: May to Oct

section: Major & Distinct Cities (new NorCal/Central Coast stops, plus out of state)
specific_attraction: Old Town Scottsdale art walk, Camelback Mountain's Echo Canyon trail, Desert Botanical Garden
why_worth_it: The shortest flight on the entire list, and pairs naturally as a stopover on the way to Sedona.
best_time: Oct to Apr, summer heat is severe

specific_attraction: Katz's, Coney Island, Yankees or Mets game, Village jazz (Village Vanguard), Brooklyn diners
why_worth_it: The point isn't the skyline — it's a pastrami counter, a ballgame and a basement jazz club in one day.
food_drink_pick: Katz's pastrami on rye; a real NY slice; Peter Luger if you book far ahead
best_time: Village Vanguard sets sell out — book online the week before.

specific_attraction: Independence Hall, Reading Terminal Market, Smithsonians (free), Arlington
why_worth_it: The Smithsonian museums are free and the Air & Space and American History collections are world-class.
food_drink_pick: Philly cheesesteak (Angelo's or John's, not the tourist two); half-smoke at Ben's Chili Bowl
best_time: Some Smithsonian venues use free timed passes — VERIFY.

specific_attraction: Broadway honky-tonks, Ryman Auditorium, Sun Studio, Stax, Graceland, Beale St blues
why_worth_it: This is the single densest music-history corridor in America — country and blues within a 3-hour drive.
food_drink_pick: Nashville hot chicken (Prince's or Hattie B's); Memphis dry-rub ribs at Rendezvous
best_time: Rent a car for the Nashville→Memphis drive; stop in Jackson or take the Natchez Trace.

specific_attraction: French Quarter, Frenchmen St jazz, Garden District streetcar, swamp tour, po'boys
why_worth_it: Frenchmen Street is where locals actually see live music; Bourbon Street is the tourist decoy.
food_drink_pick: Beignets at Café du Monde; gumbo; a Sazerac; boudin at a roadside stop
best_time: Mardi Gras (moveable, day before Ash Wednesday) transforms this stop entirely — see the events sheet.

specific_attraction: Franklin Barbecue, Lockhart BBQ trail, live music on Red River, a rodeo if in season
why_worth_it: Central Texas barbecue is a genuinely regional craft — brisket, post oak, no sauce. Lockhart is the pilgrimage.
food_drink_pick: Franklin brisket (queue at 08:00 or use the online drop); Kreuz Market; breakfast tacos
best_time: Skip Franklin's 4h queue if time-poor — La Barbecue and Interstellar are close enough.

specific_attraction: Arches, Canyonlands, Monument Valley, Antelope Canyon, Horseshoe Bend
why_worth_it: The Colorado Plateau is the one landscape type California genuinely doesn't have.
food_drink_pick: Roadside diner breakfast; Navajo taco at Monument Valley
best_time: Arches uses a timed-entry reservation system in peak months and Antelope Canyon is guide-only on Navajo land. VERIFY both.

overnight: Mackinac Island (Grand Hotel or a smaller inn)
specific_attraction: Bike or horse carriage the car free island, Grand Hotel's 660 foot porch, Original Murdick's or Ryba's fudge, Fort Mackinac
why_worth_it: Cars have been banned here since 1898; the whole island still runs on bicycles, horses and foot, which makes it feel unlike anywhere else in the Midwest route.
food_drink_pick: Fudge from a Main Street shop that still pours it on a marble slab in the window
best_time: Best May to Oct, the island largely shuts down in winter; slots into the Great Lakes leg of the 1 month USA route between Chicago and Detroit

specific_attraction: Ford Rouge Factory Tour (live F-150 line), Henry Ford Museum, Woodward Dream Cruise if mid-Aug
why_worth_it: Watching a truck body get assembled in real time is the best manufacturing tour in the country, and the museum next door holds the Rosa Parks bus and JFK's limousine.
food_drink_pick: Detroit coney dog; Slows Bar BQ
best_time: The assembly-line tour runs on production days only — VERIFY the plant schedule before booking.

specific_attraction: Indianapolis Motor Speedway Museum + track lap; NHRA U.S. Nationals if Labor Day
why_worth_it: You can ride a bus around the actual 2.5-mile oval and kiss the bricks. The museum holds a huge run of winning cars.
food_drink_pick: Indiana pork tenderloin sandwich — comically oversized, genuinely good
best_time: Time this stop to Memorial Day weekend or Labor Day if the calendar allows.

specific_attraction: Wrigley Field game, architecture river cruise, Art Institute, deep dish vs tavern-style debate
why_worth_it: The Chicago Architecture Center river cruise is the best architecture tour in America and it's from a boat.
food_drink_pick: Italian beef dipped; tavern-style thin crust (what locals actually eat); Portillo's
best_time: Wrigley bleachers on a day game is the quintessential MLB experience.

specific_attraction: Broadway honky-tonks, Ryman, Grand Ole Opry, Country Music Hall of Fame
why_worth_it: The Ryman is the mother church of country music and the acoustics are genuinely remarkable.
food_drink_pick: Hot chicken; meat-and-three at Arnold's
best_time: Opry shows rotate venues seasonally (Ryman in winter, Opry House otherwise) — VERIFY.

specific_attraction: Sloss Furnaces (preserved blast furnace), Civil Rights Institute, then an SEC football Saturday
why_worth_it: Sloss is a National Historic Landmark ironworks you can walk through — raw industrial archaeology.
food_drink_pick: Alabama white-sauce barbecue at Big Bob Gibson; Atlanta soul food at Busy Bee
best_time: The football Saturday only works Sep–Nov. Outside that, substitute the Atlanta History Center and a Braves game.

section: USA / MEX / CAN — CROSS BORDER NORTH AMERICA
specific_attraction: Stanley Park seawall bike loop, Granville Island Market, Capilano Suspension Bridge
why_worth_it: A genuinely walkable, bikeable big city with mountains and ocean both visible from downtown.
food_drink_pick: Granville Island Market food stalls
best_time: May to Sep for driest weather

section: USA / MEX / CAN — CROSS BORDER NORTH AMERICA
specific_attraction: Peak 2 Peak Gondola between two mountains, Whistler village, hiking or skiing depending on season
why_worth_it: The Sea to Sky Highway drive itself is one of the most scenic 90 minute drives in North America.
best_time: Dec to Mar skiing, Jun to Sep hiking and biking

section: USA / MEX / CAN — CROSS BORDER NORTH AMERICA
specific_attraction: Lake Louise at sunrise before the parking lot fills, Moraine Lake, Icefields Parkway drive toward Jasper
why_worth_it: Lake Louise's turquoise color comes from glacial rock flour suspended in the water, brightest on clear midsummer days.
food_drink_pick: Elk burger in Banff town
best_time: Jun to Sep, Moraine Lake road is closed most other months

section: USA / MEX / CAN — CROSS BORDER NORTH AMERICA
specific_attraction: Journey Behind the Falls, Horseshoe Falls viewpoint at night when it is lit, a Hornblower boat ride into the mist
why_worth_it: The Canadian side directly faces Horseshoe Falls; the far better photo angle compared to the US side.
best_time: May to Sep for the boat rides, illumination runs year round

section: USA / MEX / CAN — CROSS BORDER NORTH AMERICA
specific_attraction: Old Quebec walled city (the only walled city north of Mexico), Chateau Frontenac, Montmorency Falls
why_worth_it: A genuinely European feeling old town without leaving North America, cobblestone streets and all.
food_drink_pick: Poutine, tourtiere
best_time: Jun to Sep, or Dec for the Christmas market

section: USA / MEX / CAN — CROSS BORDER NORTH AMERICA
specific_attraction: Teotihuacan pyramids day trip, Frida Kahlo's Casa Azul, Chapultepec Castle, a proper taqueria crawl in Roma Norte
why_worth_it: One of the most underrated great food cities in the world, and the pyramids at Teotihuacan predate the Aztecs entirely.
food_drink_pick: Tacos al pastor, mezcal in Roma Norte
best_time: Mar to May and Sep to Nov for mild weather

section: USA / MEX / CAN — CROSS BORDER NORTH AMERICA
specific_attraction: Monte Alban ruins, mezcal tasting at a real palenque, Oaxaca City market food
why_worth_it: Oaxaca is the food and craft capital of Mexico; the mezcal here is made the way tequila used to be, at small family distilleries.
food_drink_pick: Tlayudas, mole negro
best_time: Late Oct for Dia de los Muertos, otherwise Mar to May

section: USA / MEX / CAN — CROSS BORDER NORTH AMERICA
specific_attraction: Chichen Itza, one of the New Seven Wonders of the World, at opening time before the tour buses; a nearby cenote swim afterward
why_worth_it: The El Castillo pyramid produces a famous serpent shadow illusion on the spring and fall equinoxes; on any other day, arriving at the 8am opening is the way to beat the heat and the crowds.
food_drink_pick: Cochinita pibil, fresh coconut water from a roadside stand
best_time: Equinox dates (~Mar 20, Sep 22) for the shadow effect; Nov to Feb for cooler general touring

section: USA / MEX / CAN — CROSS BORDER NORTH AMERICA
specific_attraction: Tulum ruins directly on the ocean bluff, a cenote (Gran Cenote or Dos Ojos), beach club day
why_worth_it: The only major Maya ruin site built directly overlooking the Caribbean, a genuinely different setting from the jungle sites.
food_drink_pick: Fresh ceviche on the beach
best_time: Nov to Apr for driest weather and lowest hurricane risk

section: USA / MEX / CAN — CROSS BORDER NORTH AMERICA
specific_attraction: See the Cali Whole California + Neighbors section for the full write up; repeated here since it is also the natural start of a longer Baja run down the peninsula toward Cabo
food_drink_pick: Fish tacos at Mercado Negro
best_time: Passport required for the return crossing; VERIFY current border wait times

specific_attraction: Barranco district, Larco Museum, ceviche lunch, Circuito Mágico del Agua
why_worth_it: Lima is a genuine world food city — treat it as a food stop, not a checklist stop.
food_drink_pick: Ceviche at a cevichería (lunch only — never at dinner); pisco sour; anticuchos
best_time: Central and Maido are among the world's top restaurants and book months ahead.

specific_attraction: Pisac ruins + market, Ollantaytambo fortress, Maras salt pans, Moray terraces
why_worth_it: Moray's concentric agricultural terraces have measurably different microclimates per level — Inca agronomic engineering.
food_drink_pick: Cuy if you're curious; quinoa soup; chicha morada
best_time: Sleep in the valley (2,800m) not Cusco (3,400m) on arrival night — it materially reduces altitude sickness.

specific_attraction: Machu Picchu citadel — pick your circuit; Huayna Picchu or Huchuy Picchu add-on
why_worth_it: The site is managed by timed circuits now, and which circuit you buy determines what you actually get to see.
best_time: Entry is by specific circuit + time slot, capped daily, and sells out weeks ahead in dry season. VERIFY the current circuit rules — they have changed more than once.

transport: Tourist bus (with stops) or overnight bus
specific_attraction: Uros floating reed islands, Taquile Island homestay
why_worth_it: The Uros islands are genuinely built from floating totora reed. It's touristed but the engineering is real.
food_drink_pick: Trucha (lake trout)
best_time: The daytime tourist bus with archaeological stops beats the overnight bus — the route is the sightseeing.

specific_attraction: Mi Teleférico cable-car network, Witches' Market, Valle de la Luna, Death Road MTB (optional)
why_worth_it: The cable-car system is the world's largest urban aerial network and functions as actual public transit at 3,600m — an extraordinary piece of infrastructure.
food_drink_pick: Salteñas for breakfast; api con pastel
best_time: VERIFY Bolivian entry requirements for US passports before committing — they have changed repeatedly.

specific_attraction: Salt flats, Isla Incahuasi, coloured lagoons, Sol de Mañana geysers, border into Chile
why_worth_it: The world's largest salt flat, then two days across 4,000m+ altiplano to the Chilean border. One of the great overland journeys.
food_drink_pick: Basic tour food — bring snacks
best_time: Accommodation on the crossing is genuinely basic (shared rooms, limited heating, no reliable power). Choose a licensed operator with oxygen and radio. Solo-version item; partner version excludes this.

route: Uyuni/Atacama corridor → Rio (separate flight, this is the Atlantic corridor, not a drive on from the Andean leg)
transport: Flight (likely via Sao Paulo or Santiago)
specific_attraction: Christ the Redeemer at Corcovado (go early or take the van up, not the crowded midday train), Sugarloaf cable car at sunset, Selaron Steps
why_worth_it: One of the New Seven Wonders of the World and the single most recognizable statue in the Americas; the view over Guanabara Bay from the base is worth the crowds.
food_drink_pick: Feijoada on a Saturday, a proper churrascaria dinner
best_time: Rio does not connect efficiently to the Andean corridor (Peru/Bolivia/Chile) in the same trip; treat it as the anchor of the separate Atlantic corridor mentioned in the brief, or the Solo 1 month extension

specific_attraction: Westminster + Borough Market + Sky Garden (free, booked)
why_worth_it: Sky Garden is the free alternative to the Shard with a better room. Borough is the food anchor.
food_drink_pick: Borough Market: Kappacasein raclette toastie, Bread Ahead doughnut
best_time: Sky Garden slots free but released ~3 weeks ahead and go fast.

specific_attraction: Louvre, Musée d'Orsay, Sainte-Chapelle, Montmartre
why_worth_it: Sainte-Chapelle's glass is the single most underrated 45 minutes in Paris.
food_drink_pick: Boulangerie breakfast; a proper bistro dinner in the 11e
best_time: Eurostar needs passport control — arrive 60–75 min early.

specific_attraction: Rijksmuseum, canal ring walk, Zaanse Schans, Keukenhof (seasonal)
why_worth_it: Keukenhof is only open ~8 weeks a year and is the reason to time the trip to April.
food_drink_pick: Stroopwafel made fresh; haring from a street cart
best_time: Keukenhof roughly late Mar–mid May. VERIFY the year's dates.

specific_attraction: Berlin Wall Memorial, Museum Island, Topography of Terror, Teufelsberg
why_worth_it: Teufelsberg is a Cold War NSA listening station on a rubble hill — legal, ticketed, covered in street art.
food_drink_pick: Currywurst, döner (Berlin invented the modern one), Turkish market on Maybachufer
best_time: Overnight train Amsterdam→Berlin exists via European Sleeper — VERIFY current routing.

specific_attraction: Old Town, Charles Bridge at dawn, Prague Castle, Vyšehrad
why_worth_it: Charles Bridge at 06:00 vs 11:00 is the difference between a masterpiece and a market.
food_drink_pick: Trdelník is a tourist invention — eat svíčková and drink Pilsner instead
best_time: The Berlin→Prague train follows the Elbe gorge and is one of Europe's best cheap scenic rides.

specific_attraction: Vienna Ring + Schönbrunn; day trip to Hallstatt
why_worth_it: Hallstatt is the most Instagram-saturated village in Europe. It is genuinely beautiful at 07:00 and unbearable at 11:00.
food_drink_pick: Sachertorte, Naschmarkt, a proper Viennese coffee house sit
best_time: Hallstatt has installed anti-selfie barriers and caps coach traffic. Go early or stay overnight.

specific_attraction: Jungfrau region: Lauterbrunnen, Mürren, Schilthorn, Grindelwald First
why_worth_it: Lauterbrunnen valley with 72 waterfalls is the single best mountain-day in Europe by rail.
food_drink_pick: Fondue in Mürren; rösti
best_time: Switzerland roughly doubles your daily spend. Swiss Travel Pass usually pays off here.

specific_attraction: Galeries Lafayette Haussmann rooftop terrace and the stained glass dome inside, both free with no ticket or reservation
why_worth_it: A free 360 degree rooftop view of the Paris skyline including the Eiffel Tower and Opera Garnier, with zero line and zero ticket, inside a working department store.
food_drink_pick: Lafayette Gourmet food hall in the basement
best_time: Year round, go near opening or just before closing to avoid the shop floor crowds

specific_attraction: Westminster, British Museum, Tower, Camden, Sky Garden, Soho
why_worth_it: British Museum is free and enormous — pick three galleries, don't attempt it all.
food_drink_pick: Sunday roast; Brick Lane salt-beef bagel at 2am
best_time: Most national museums are free.

specific_attraction: Louvre, Orsay, Sainte-Chapelle, Eiffel, Montmartre, Le Marais
why_worth_it: Three days is the minimum for Paris to stop feeling like a checklist.
food_drink_pick: Croissant at Du Pain et des Idées; steak-frites in the 11e
best_time: Notre-Dame reopened Dec 2024 — free entry but timed reservation strongly advised.

specific_attraction: D-Day beaches: Omaha, Pointe du Hoc, American Cemetery, Bayeux Tapestry
why_worth_it: Pointe du Hoc still has the craters and bunkers untouched. A guided full-day is genuinely better here — the terrain needs narration.
food_drink_pick: Camembert, cider, Norman butter; moules at Port-en-Bessin
best_time: Mont-Saint-Michel is 1h15 further and is the region's other must — best at low tide or overnight after the coaches leave.

specific_attraction: Wall Memorial, Museum Island, Topography of Terror, Teufelsberg, Tempelhof
why_worth_it: Tempelhof: a disused Nazi-era airport whose runways are now a public park you can cycle down.
food_drink_pick: Döner at Mustafa's; currywurst; Turkish market Fri on Maybachufer
best_time: Berlin is the cheapest major city in this itinerary by a wide margin.

specific_attraction: Sagrada Família, Park Güell, Casa Batlló, Gothic Quarter, Bunkers del Carmel
why_worth_it: Sagrada Família's towers are being completed — the interior light through the columns is the actual attraction, not the facade.
food_drink_pick: Vermut hour; Bar del Pla; a proper seafood paella (never on La Rambla)
best_time: Sagrada Família timed tickets sell out days ahead. Tower access is a separate add-on.

specific_attraction: Prado, Retiro, San Miguel market; AVE to Seville (Alcázar, Cathedral) and Granada (Alhambra)
why_worth_it: The Alhambra is the single best building in this itinerary and needs a ticket bought weeks out.
food_drink_pick: Jamón ibérico de bellota; salmorejo; Seville tapas crawl in Triana
best_time: Alhambra Nasrid Palaces have a hard timed entry slot and sell out 1–2 months ahead in high season.

specific_attraction: Shibuya Scramble Crossing (ground level + Starbucks Tsutaya window)
why_worth_it: The single most-filmed intersection on earth. Do it at ground level first, elevated second — the contrast is the point.
food_drink_pick: Ichiran Shibuya (solo ramen booths) — the classic first-night meal
best_time: Best density ~19:00–21:00 on a weekday. Rain nights are BETTER — the reflections are why the cinematic shots look the way they do.

specific_attraction: Shibuya Sky — open-air rooftop deck, 47F
why_worth_it: The only major Tokyo deck that is genuinely open-air, with the crossing directly below and Fuji on the horizon on clear winter days.
best_time: Sunset slots sell out ~4 weeks ahead. Book the slot ~40 min BEFORE sunset so you get daylight, golden hour and night in one ticket.

specific_attraction: Hachiko statue + Shibuya Yokocho / Nonbei Yokocho alley bars
why_worth_it: Nonbei Yokocho is the surviving postwar alley — two-seat bars, still local, 3 min from the world's busiest crossing.
food_drink_pick: Standing sake at a Nonbei counter
best_time: Solo travellers do far better here than groups — many bars seat 4.

specific_attraction: Meiji Jingu — approach forest, torii, sake barrel wall
why_worth_it: A 100-year-old planted forest engineered to look primeval, 200m from the loudest teen street in Asia. The whiplash is the experience.
best_time: Go at opening (sunrise-linked, varies monthly). Weekend mornings sometimes have Shinto wedding processions in the main courtyard.

specific_attraction: Takeshita Street + Cat Street + Omotesando architecture walk
why_worth_it: Takeshita is 15 minutes of sensory overload; Cat Street and Omotesando are where the actual buying happens. Omotesando is an open-air museum of Pritzker-winner facades (Tod's, Prada, Dior).
food_drink_pick: Marion Crepes / Zaku Zaku croquant — the viral Takeshita food
best_time: For an EE brain: the Prada Aoyama diamond-grid facade is structurally load-bearing glass, not cladding. Worth 10 min just looking up.

specific_attraction: Suga Shrine staircase — 'Your Name' final scene
why_worth_it: The exact staircase from the last shot of Kimi no Na wa. Two minutes to shoot, and it sits in a quiet residential pocket most tourists never enter.
best_time: Residential street. Locals live here — no tripods, no blocking the stairs, keep voices down.

specific_attraction: Omoide Yokocho + Golden Gai + Kabukicho / Godzilla head
why_worth_it: Omoide Yokocho ('Piss Alley') is grilled-offal smoke and postwar tin roofing; Golden Gai is 200+ six-seat themed bars in six alleys.
food_drink_pick: Yakitori + lemon sour at an Omoide Yokocho counter
best_time: Many Golden Gai bars charge a ¥500–1,500 seat charge; English-friendly ones post it on the door. Some are locals-only — respect it.

specific_attraction: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building free observatory
why_worth_it: Free 202m view, and since 2023 the building's face hosts a nightly projection-mapping show (Guinness-record scale).
best_time: Free vs. Shibuya Sky ¥2,500 — skip if you already did Shibuya Sky unless you want the projection show.

specific_attraction: Senso-ji, Kaminarimon, Nakamise-dori
why_worth_it: Tokyo's oldest temple (founded 645). At 06:30 you get the main hall with almost nobody in it; by 10:00 Nakamise is a river of people.
food_drink_pick: Melonpan from Kagetsudo; ningyo-yaki off Nakamise
best_time: Grounds are open 24h; main hall 06:00–17:00. The sunrise version of this visit is a completely different attraction.

specific_attraction: Tokyo Skytree + Sumida River / Asahi Building view
why_worth_it: 634m, tallest tower in the world. Honestly better photographed from the Sumida riverbank than ascended — unless the air is winter-clear.
best_time: If you already booked Shibuya Sky, treat Skytree as a photo subject, not a ticket. Skip the ascent unless visibility is excellent.

specific_attraction: Akihabara Electric Town — Super Potato, Mandarake, Yodobashi, Radio Kaikan
why_worth_it: For a hardware person this is the actual attraction: the back-alley parts shops under the tracks still sell discrete components, connectors and dev boards by the bin.
food_drink_pick: Kanda Matsuya soba (nearby, 1884) or a standing curry
best_time: Go under the Sobu line viaduct to the parts market (Tokyo Radio Depart / Akihabara Radio Center) — that's the pre-anime Akihabara and it's directly relevant to your bench work.

specific_attraction: teamLab Planets TOKYO (barefoot, water rooms)
why_worth_it: Genuinely the best of the digital-art venues — you walk through knee-deep water and a mirrored infinity room. Not a passive exhibit.
best_time: teamLab operates multiple venues (Planets in Toyosu, Borderless in Azabudai Hills). VERIFY which is open on your dates — venues have moved before. Wear shorts or roll-ups; you get wet to the knee.

specific_attraction: Unicorn Gundam statue transformation + DiverCity
why_worth_it: 19.7m Unicorn that mechanically transforms on a schedule with lighting. The Gundam Base store above it is the real pilgrimage.
best_time: Transformation happens several times daily + a night light show. VERIFY the current schedule board — it changes seasonally.

transport: JR Limited Express Fuji Excursion / Highway bus
specific_attraction: The 'Mt Fuji Lawson' shot (Lawson Kawaguchiko-ekimae)
why_worth_it: The konbini-under-Fuji frame that defined Japan travel TikTok in 2022–24. It is one photo, and it is genuinely a good one.
food_drink_pick: Buy something in the store — it's courtesy, not a rule
best_time: Barrier status has flip-flopped repeatedly: 2.5m black screen May 2024, removed Aug 2024, ~1.4m brown barrier Aug 2025, reportedly gone again as of Aug 2026. CHECK before you build a morning around it. Never cross mid-road or climb anything — that behaviour is exactly why the screens went up.

transport: JR Limited Express Fuji Excursion / Highway bus
specific_attraction: Chureito Pagoda, Arakurayama Sengen Park (398 steps)
why_worth_it: The pagoda-plus-Fuji-plus-cherry-blossom frame. Objectively the best single Fuji composition that exists, and worth the stairs.
best_time: Peak is early–mid April (sakura) and mid-November (foliage). Sunrise gives you side-light on the pagoda; midday flattens it completely.

transport: JR Limited Express Fuji Excursion / Highway bus
specific_attraction: Honcho-dori street — Fuji framed down the road
why_worth_it: The retro shopping street with Fuji sitting at the end of it. Shot from the pedestrian crossing, telephoto compresses the mountain enormously.
food_drink_pick: Fujiyoshida udon — thick, brutally chewy, a genuine regional oddity
best_time: This is a live road with a bus route. Shoot from the sidewalk/crossing only. 70–200mm equivalent is the difference between 'nice' and 'the viral shot'.

transport: JR Limited Express Fuji Excursion / Highway bus
specific_attraction: Lake Kawaguchiko north shore + Oishi Park
why_worth_it: Reflection ('Sakasa-Fuji') on windless mornings, plus seasonal flower beds — kochia turning red in October is the underrated one.
food_drink_pick: Hoto noodle hotpot (Kosaku) — the Yamanashi dish
best_time: Reflection needs a windless morning. Fuji is statistically most visible Nov–Feb and least visible in June–Aug haze.

specific_attraction: ACADEMIC HALF-DAY: Narusawa Ice Cave & Fugaku Wind Cave, marked lava-forest trail
why_worth_it: For your humanities report: the established, ticketed visitor caves and the maintained interpretive trail let you study the actual subject — the 864 AD Jogan eruption, the lava-flow ecology, and how the forest became a media object — without leaving the formal route.
best_time: Daylight only, stay on marked/interpretive trails, go with a licensed local guide or ranger-led route if you can. This is a real ecosystem study site: the lava substrate suppresses soil depth, which is why roots grow laterally and the tree density looks the way it does. Do NOT film or seek out anything relating to deaths; signage asks visitors not to, local authorities enforce it, and it has nothing to do with the ecology or the historical record you are writing about.

specific_attraction: Framing sources for the report: Saiko Iyashi-no-Sato Nenba (restored thatched village + local history museum)
why_worth_it: Gives you the human/settlement side of the same lava plateau — how people actually lived on this ground — which is what turns a 'creepy forest' essay into a real humanities paper.
food_drink_pick: Local hoto and mountain vegetables
best_time: Pair primary observation here with published sources on the Jogan eruption, Edo-period Fuji pilgrimage routes, and the 1960s literary/media construction of the forest's reputation. That last strand is the strongest thesis available and avoids sensationalism entirely.

specific_attraction: Transfer to Hakone, evening onsen
why_worth_it: Ends a heavy research day in hot water. Hakone has been a working hot-spring town since the 8th century.
food_drink_pick: Kaiseki dinner at the ryokan
best_time: Kawaguchiko→Hakone is awkward by rail; the direct Fujikyu/Odakyu highway bus is usually the sane option. VERIFY current bus timetable.

transport: Hakone Free Pass: train, cable, ropeway, boat
specific_attraction: Hakone Round Course: switchback railway → cable car → ropeway → pirate boat
why_worth_it: Five transport modes in one loop, each with a different view of the caldera. It's a transport-nerd itinerary disguised as sightseeing.
food_drink_pick: Owakudani kuro-tamago — eggs boiled black in sulphur springs
best_time: Owakudani ropeway section closes on volcanic gas readings, sometimes at short notice. VERIFY status the morning of.

transport: Hakone Free Pass: train, cable, ropeway, boat
specific_attraction: Hakone Shrine lake torii (Heiwa-no-Torii)
why_worth_it: Vermilion torii standing in Lake Ashi with Fuji behind it on a clear day. The queue for the photo is famously long and famously orderly.
best_time: Photo queue can hit 60+ min by 10:00. Before 08:00 it's nearly empty.

transport: Hakone Free Pass: train, cable, ropeway, boat
specific_attraction: Hakone Open-Air Museum
why_worth_it: Sculpture on a mountainside with a Picasso pavilion and a stained-glass tower. Better than it sounds and a genuine alternative to another shrine.
best_time: Good rain contingency for this day.

specific_attraction: Fushimi Inari Taisha — full ridge climb to Ichinomine
why_worth_it: 10,000+ torii. Everyone photographs the first 400m; the actual experience is the 2-hour loop above the Yotsutsuji junction where the crowd evaporates.
food_drink_pick: Grilled quail / sparrow at the approach stalls (a real Fushimi oddity)
best_time: Open 24h, unstaffed at night. 06:00–07:30 is the difference between a shrine and a queue.

specific_attraction: Kiyomizu-dera + Sannenzaka / Ninenzaka approach
why_worth_it: The 13m wooden stage, built with zero nails, over a hillside. The preserved sloping lanes below it are the most photographed streets in Japan.
food_drink_pick: Yatsuhashi (raw cinnamon mochi) and matcha soft-serve on Ninenzaka
best_time: Photography is banned on parts of Ninenzaka by city ordinance and fines apply on private lanes. Read the posted signs.

specific_attraction: Gion — Hanamikoji, Shirakawa canal, Yasaka Pagoda (Hokan-ji)
why_worth_it: Shirakawa canal at dusk is the quieter, better-looking half of Gion. The Yasaka Pagoda framed down Yasaka-dori is the postcard.
food_drink_pick: Kyoto obanzai + a Pontocho riverside counter
best_time: Private alleys off Hanamikoji are closed to tourists with a ¥10,000 fine posted. Never photograph geiko/maiko without permission — it's the specific behaviour that got the alleys closed.

specific_attraction: Bamboo Grove + Okochi Sanso villa garden
why_worth_it: The grove is 10 minutes and heaving by 09:00. Okochi Sanso next door has better views, a matcha included, and 5% of the people.
best_time: Bamboo grove before 07:00 or don't bother. Okochi Sanso is the one I'd actually keep.

specific_attraction: Sagano Romantic Train (Torokko) + Hozugawa river boat
why_worth_it: Open-sided vintage train through a gorge, then a 2-hour boat back down the rapids. One of Japan's best scenic transport pairings.
best_time: Torokko closes for winter (roughly late Dec–Feb) and sells out in foliage season. VERIFY dates + book ahead.

specific_attraction: Kinkaku-ji → Ryoan-ji rock garden
why_worth_it: Gold pavilion is a 25-minute one-way walk you cannot skip once. Ryoan-ji's 15-stone garden is the one that actually rewards sitting still.
best_time: Kinkaku-ji is a conveyor belt. Ryoan-ji is where you'd put the extra 30 minutes.

specific_attraction: Nishiki Market + Nintendo Museum (Uji)
why_worth_it: Nishiki is 400m of prepared food. The Nintendo Museum (opened Oct 2024, in the old Uji plant) is a serious company-history museum, not a gift shop.
food_drink_pick: Tako-tamago, tofu doughnuts, uni at Nishiki
best_time: Nintendo Museum tickets are a lottery/advance system and sell out far ahead — apply the month you fix your dates. This is a MUST specifically for you.

specific_attraction: Todai-ji Daibutsu + Nara Park deer + Kasuga Taisha lanterns
why_worth_it: The Great Buddha Hall is one of the largest wooden buildings on earth and the 15m bronze inside it is genuinely staggering in person.
food_drink_pick: Nakatanidou mochi pounding (the viral high-speed one)
best_time: Deer bow for crackers and will absolutely mug you for a paper map. Kasuga Taisha's 3,000 lanterns are lit only a few nights a year — VERIFY.

specific_attraction: Dotonbori — Glico sign, Ebisu bridge, Hozenji Yokocho
why_worth_it: Loud, neon, and unapologetically about eating. Hozenji Yokocho two streets away is the moss-covered opposite and takes 10 minutes.
food_drink_pick: Takoyaki (Wanaka), kushikatsu in Shinsekai — never double-dip the sauce
best_time: The 'no double-dipping' rule at kushikatsu counters is real and locals will tell you.

specific_attraction: Shinsekai + Tsutenkaku tower
why_worth_it: 1912 vision of the future, now beautifully shabby. The most un-Instagram part of Osaka and better for it.
food_drink_pick: Kushikatsu, doteyaki
best_time: Good late-night wander if you still have energy after Dotonbori.

specific_attraction: Universal Studios Japan — Super Nintendo World
why_worth_it: The Mario land is a genuine engineering achievement — the wearable Power-Up Band turns the whole area into a playable interface.
best_time: Needs a timed Area Ticket even with park admission. Buy Express Pass or accept 90+ min queues. Skip entirely if you'd rather have the Kobe/Ikeda day below.

specific_attraction: Cup Noodles Museum Osaka Ikeda — make your own cup
why_worth_it: You design the cup, choose four toppings, and it's sealed in front of you. Free entry, tiny fee for the cup. Absurdly good value.
food_drink_pick: Your own instant ramen, obviously
best_time: The Chicken Ramen hands-on workshop (making noodles from scratch) needs advance reservation and is the better version if you can get it.

specific_attraction: Kobe beef teppanyaki + Nunobiki Herb Garden ropeway + harbour night view
why_worth_it: Kobe is 20 min from Osaka and gives you a completely different city texture — port, hills, and the best-known beef in the world.
food_drink_pick: A5 Kobe beef (book ahead — walk-ins at good places are hard)
best_time: Proper Kobe beef teppanyaki runs ¥15,000–30,000. Lunch sets at the same restaurants are often half price for the same grade.

transport: JR Hashidate LtdExp / Kyoto Tango Railway
specific_attraction: Amanohashidate sandbar + Kasamatsu Park 'matanozoki' viewpoint
why_worth_it: One of Japan's official Three Views. The tradition is to look at it upside-down through your legs so the sandbar reads as a dragon in the sky.
food_drink_pick: Grilled seafood; local Tango sake
best_time: Rent a bicycle and ride the sandbar itself — 3.6km through pines. That's the part most day-trippers skip.

transport: JR Hashidate LtdExp / Kyoto Tango Railway
specific_attraction: Ine no Funaya — boathouses built over the water
why_worth_it: 230 boathouses with garages at sea level and living quarters above. Best seen from the sightseeing boat or a kayak, not the road.
food_drink_pick: Ine sake brewery (Mukai Shuzo — female toji, red 'Ine Mankai' rice sake)
best_time: This is exactly the kind of place that justifies the transfer. Bus from Amanohashidate ~1h.

transport: JR Hashidate LtdExp / Kyoto Tango Railway
specific_attraction: Maizuru Red Brick Park (Meiji naval warehouses)
why_worth_it: Twelve preserved 1900s red-brick naval warehouses — Japan's industrial-military architecture, and a filming location regular.
best_time: Only worth it if the rail timing puts you through Nishi-Maizuru anyway.

transport: Shinkansen to Okayama + JR Shiokaze LtdExp
specific_attraction: Dogo Onsen Honkan — the historically significant onsen
why_worth_it: Referenced in the Nihon Shoki, so arguably the oldest continuously used hot spring in Japan. The 1894 wooden bathhouse is the one that inspired Spirited Away's bathhouse look.
food_drink_pick: Botchan dango; Dogo beer
best_time: Honkan finished a long phased restoration; tiers of tickets (basic bath vs. upstairs tatami rest room + tea). Take the upper tier once — that's the actual historical experience.

transport: Shinkansen to Okayama + JR Shiokaze LtdExp
specific_attraction: Matsuyama Castle (ropeway or hill climb)
why_worth_it: One of only twelve original surviving keeps in Japan — not a concrete postwar rebuild. That distinction matters and most castle photos you've seen are rebuilds.
food_drink_pick: Taimeshi (sea bream rice), jakoten fish cake
best_time: Twelve original keeps: Matsuyama, Matsue, Hikone, Himeji, Inuyama, Kochi, Marugame, Uwajima, Bitchu-Matsuyama, Maruoka, Hirosaki, Matsumoto.

transport: Shinkansen to Okayama + JR Shiokaze LtdExp
specific_attraction: Uchiko Yokaichi historic street + Uchikoza kabuki theatre; Ozu Castle
why_worth_it: Uchiko got rich on wax production; the merchant street and the 1916 wooden kabuki theatre survived intact. Ozu adds a fully reconstructed wooden castle keep.
best_time: Solo-only pick. Two similar historic towns back to back is exactly the redundancy the partner version cuts.

transport: Uwajima Unyu ferry across the Bungo Channel
specific_attraction: Beppu Hells (Umi Jigoku, Chinoike Jigoku) + steam-vent townscape
why_worth_it: Beppu produces more hot-spring water than anywhere in Japan except Yellowstone globally. The whole town steams from the drains.
food_drink_pick: Jigoku-mushi — steam-cooked seafood and vegetables you cook yourself in a vent
best_time: Two hells (Umi = cobalt blue, Chinoike = blood red) are enough. The 7-hell combo ticket is a redundancy trap.

transport: Uwajima Unyu ferry across the Bungo Channel
specific_attraction: Myoban Onsen yunohana huts + a proper sand bath (Beppu Kaihin Sunayu)
why_worth_it: Buried to the neck in naturally heated black sand on the beach. Genuinely strange and genuinely relaxing.
best_time: Sand bath is ~10–15 min buried; you wear a provided yukata. Bring a towel.

transport: Uwajima Unyu ferry across the Bungo Channel
specific_attraction: Yufuin — Kinrin Lake morning mist, Yunotsubo street
why_worth_it: Kinrin Lake steams at dawn in cold months because hot springs feed it. Yunotsubo street is very touristy — the lake at 07:00 is the real reason to come.
food_drink_pick: Yufuin Milch cheesecake; B-Speak roll cake
best_time: The mist needs cold air + water temp differential — best Nov–Feb mornings.

route: Beppu → Hakata → HND/NRT or FUK out
specific_attraction: Dazaifu Tenmangu + Starbucks Dazaifu (Kengo Kuma)
why_worth_it: Shrine to the god of learning, plus Kengo Kuma's woven-timber Starbucks on the approach — 2,000 interlocking sticks, no nails in the lattice.
food_drink_pick: Umegae-mochi, grilled fresh on the approach
best_time: Main hall has been under a multi-year rebuild with a striking temporary 'floating forest' shrine designed by Sou Fujimoto. VERIFY which structure is standing on your dates — the temporary one is arguably more interesting.

route: Beppu → Hakata → HND/NRT or FUK out
specific_attraction: Nakasu yatai (riverside street-food stalls)
why_worth_it: Japan's last real concentration of open-air yatai stalls. Ten seats, shoulder to shoulder, tonkotsu steam. Peak solo travel.
food_drink_pick: Hakata tonkotsu ramen (kaedama refill), mentaiko tamagoyaki, yakitori
best_time: Yatai open ~18:00, close in rain and typhoons. Cash is king. Some are locals-only; look for posted English menus.

route: Beppu → Hakata → HND/NRT or FUK out
specific_attraction: Canal City / Fukuoka Tower or a last Ohori Park walk before flight
why_worth_it: Low-effort buffer block before departure so a delayed train doesn't cost you the flight.
food_drink_pick: Final bowl of Ichiran (the original Fukuoka chain)
best_time: Fly out of FUK rather than backtracking to Tokyo — usually cheaper in time than the 5h Shinkansen.

specific_attraction: Peace Memorial Museum + A-Bomb Dome + Peace Park
why_worth_it: The museum is deliberately, unflinchingly hard. It is the single most important museum visit in Japan and you should give it a full unhurried block.
food_drink_pick: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (layered, with noodles) at Okonomimura
best_time: Go early; school groups arrive mid-morning. Allow decompression time afterwards — don't schedule anything demanding right after.

specific_attraction: Itsukushima Shrine floating torii + Mt Misen ropeway/hike
why_worth_it: The torii only 'floats' at high tide; at low tide you walk out to its base. Two entirely different photographs, both worth having.
food_drink_pick: Grilled oysters; momiji manju
best_time: Check the tide table before choosing your ferry time — it decides which version you get. A separate ¥100 visitor tax applies to the ferry.

specific_attraction: Kenrokuen garden + Higashi Chaya district + 21st Century Museum
why_worth_it: One of the Three Great Gardens; the gold-leaf teahouse district survived the war intact. SANAA's circular glass museum is a Pritzker landmark.
food_drink_pick: Omicho Market kaisendon; gold-leaf soft serve (yes, really)
best_time: Kanazawa is the single best 'second city' in Japan and most 2-week itineraries can't fit it. This is why the 1-month exists.

specific_attraction: Gassho-zukuri thatched village + Shiroyama viewpoint
why_worth_it: Steep-thatched farmhouses built to shed 3m of snow. The winter illumination nights are one of Japan's genuinely great sights.
food_drink_pick: Hida beef skewers
best_time: Winter light-up is a handful of nights in Jan–Feb, reservation-only and heavily oversubscribed. VERIFY dates the previous autumn.

specific_attraction: Ghibli Park — Grand Warehouse, Valley of Witches, Mononoke Village
why_worth_it: Not a theme park with rides — it's a set of buildings you walk into. The Grand Warehouse is the essential one.
best_time: Date-and-time tickets sold by advance lottery months ahead, area-by-area. This is one of the hardest tickets in Japan — plan the trip around the ticket, not the reverse.

specific_attraction: Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology
why_worth_it: Live working looms and machine tools running on the floor, tracing textile machinery into automotive manufacturing. Straight into your engineering interests.
food_drink_pick: Nagoya miso katsu; hitsumabushi eel
best_time: Pair with Toyota Automobile Museum (separate site, Nagakute) if you want the car collection rather than the manufacturing story.

specific_attraction: Matsushima Bay — 260 pine islands, Godaido, Zuiganji
why_worth_it: The second of the Three Views. Best experienced from the bay cruise or the Saigyo Modoshi hilltop, not the waterfront car park.
food_drink_pick: Grilled oysters (winter); zunda (edamame) shake in Sendai
best_time: Oyster season roughly Oct–Mar. Bay cruises cancel in high wind.

specific_attraction: Tsuruga Castle + Sazaedo double-helix pagoda + Ouchi-juku
why_worth_it: Sazaedo is an 18th-century wooden temple with two independent spiral ramps so ascending and descending visitors never meet — an architectural oddity that genuinely predates the modern double helix.
food_drink_pick: Kitakata ramen; Aizu sauce-katsudon
best_time: Sazaedo is exactly the weird-over-famous pick you said you value. Ouchi-juku is a thatched post-town, spectacular under snow.

specific_attraction: Nebuta Warasse museum (year-round) — or Nebuta Matsuri if timing aligns
why_worth_it: Giant illuminated warrior floats. Warasse keeps prize-winning floats on display all year, so the trip works even outside the festival.
food_drink_pick: Nokkedon (build-your-own sashimi bowl) at Furukawa Market
best_time: Nebuta Matsuri runs Aug 2–7 annually (fixed dates). If your trip is in early August, restructure the entire itinerary around it — it's that good. Accommodation sells out ~6+ months ahead.

specific_attraction: Hirosaki Castle (original keep) + castle park
why_worth_it: Another of the twelve original keeps, and the best cherry-blossom castle park in Japan — petals carpet the moat.
food_drink_pick: Apple pie — Hirosaki is Japan's apple capital and has a whole apple-pie guide map
best_time: Blossom here is late April/early May, well after Tokyo — which is exactly how you chase sakura twice in one trip.

specific_attraction: Mt Hakodate night view + Motomachi slopes + Goryokaku star fort
why_worth_it: The night view from Mt Hakodate is ranked among Japan's best. Goryokaku is a Western-style star fort — unique in Japan and best from its tower.
food_drink_pick: Hakodate morning market squid — you can fish your own; uni and kaisendon
best_time: The Seikan Tunnel crossing itself is a landmark piece of civil engineering: 53.85km, 23.3km undersea.

specific_attraction: Sapporo Beer Museum + Nijo Market + Susukino nightlife
why_worth_it: Japan's oldest beer brand in its original brick brewhouse, with a tasting flight of beers you can't buy elsewhere.
food_drink_pick: Miso ramen (Sapporo style), soup curry, Genghis Khan lamb BBQ
best_time: Soup curry is a Sapporo invention and underrated internationally.

specific_attraction: Otaru Canal + Sakaimachi glassworks + Tenguyama
why_worth_it: Gas-lamplit canal warehouses. In February the Snow Light Path festival lines it with candle lanterns and it becomes genuinely magical.
food_drink_pick: Otaru sushi street; LeTAO double fromage cheesecake
best_time: Snow Light Path is ~10 days in February. Sapporo Snow Festival is early Feb — the two overlap and that week is the strongest winter argument for Hokkaido.

specific_attraction: Tokyo DisneySea
why_worth_it: Widely considered the best-designed theme park in the world — DisneySea exists nowhere else, and Fantasy Springs added a whole new port.
best_time: Buy tickets the moment your date is fixed. Consider the Disney Premier Access for the newest attractions.

specific_attraction: Sumo tournament (if in season) or a NPB baseball game at Jingu/Tokyo Dome
why_worth_it: Grand sumo runs six 15-day tournaments a year, three of them in Tokyo (Jan, May, Sep). Baseball with a Yakult crowd is the other great Japanese spectator experience.
food_drink_pick: Chanko-nabe in Ryogoku
best_time: Tokyo basho: January, May, September. Osaka March, Nagoya July, Fukuoka November. VERIFY exact dates; tickets go on sale ~1 month ahead and sell fast.

specific_attraction: Easy arrival: Shibuya Sky at sunset, then dinner
why_worth_it: One high-impact thing on arrival day and nothing else. Jet lag is the enemy of the rest of the trip.
food_drink_pick: Omakase sushi or a quiet izakaya — not a queue restaurant
best_time: Deliberately under-scheduled. This is the structural difference between the two trip types.

transport: Metro + taxi where it saves an hour
specific_attraction: Meiji Jingu early, then Omotesando + Cat Street
why_worth_it: Forest, then design street, then coffee. One neighbourhood, no cross-city transit.
food_drink_pick: Koffee Mameya; a proper Omotesando lunch
best_time: Takeshita Street is CUT here — it's crowded, teen-focused, and adds nothing the rest of the day doesn't.

transport: Metro + taxi where it saves an hour
specific_attraction: teamLab Planets, evening
why_worth_it: Shared, physical, memorable and photographs beautifully as a couple. Best single 'experience' venue in Tokyo.
best_time: Book the earliest evening slot; wear clothes you can roll above the knee.

specific_attraction: Asakusa at sunrise (Senso-ji empty), then Sumida riverside coffee
why_worth_it: The 06:30 version is peaceful and romantic. The 11:00 version is a scrum. Same place, opposite experience.
food_drink_pick: Asakusa melonpan; Suzukien Asakusa — the world's strongest matcha gelato (7 levels)
best_time: Skytree ascent CUT — you'll have had Shibuya Sky, and a second tower is pure redundancy.

specific_attraction: Yanaka Ginza + Nezu Shrine torii tunnel — old-Tokyo afternoon
why_worth_it: The low-rise, cat-filled, pre-war neighbourhood that survived the bombing. Nezu's miniature torii tunnel is Fushimi Inari without the crowd.
food_drink_pick: Menchi-katsu on Yanaka Ginza; Kayaba Coffee
best_time: This replaces Akihabara in the partner version — same 'real Tokyo' payoff, far more pleasant to share.

specific_attraction: Romancecar front-row seats + Hakone Open-Air Museum
why_worth_it: The Romancecar's panoramic front seats are a small, cheap, genuinely delightful thing. The museum is sculpture on a mountainside.
best_time: Front observation seats are limited and released ~1 month ahead. Book the second the window opens.

specific_attraction: Ryokan with in-room or private open-air bath + kaiseki dinner
why_worth_it: The single best thing you can spend money on in Japan as a couple. A private rotenburo removes the tattoo/modesty issue entirely.
food_drink_pick: Multi-course kaiseki with local Ashigara beef
best_time: ¥40,000–90,000+ per room per night with two meals. Book 3–6 months out for foliage season. This is the one line item worth overspending on.

specific_attraction: Chureito Pagoda at sunrise + Oishi Park lakeside
why_worth_it: Do the two best Fuji viewpoints and stop. You do not need five.
food_drink_pick: Hoto hotpot at Kosaku
best_time: Honcho-dori street shot and the Lawson shot are both CUT here — same mountain, same light, marginal return, and the Lawson spot has a genuine crowd/etiquette problem.

specific_attraction: Lake-view onsen room + Kachi Kachi ropeway at sunset
why_worth_it: Waking up with Fuji in the window is the memory. The ropeway is 3 minutes and gives you the lake-and-mountain frame together.
best_time: Fuji visibility is far better Nov–Feb. If your dates are June–August, book flexible and treat a clear Fuji as a bonus.

specific_attraction: Gion Shirakawa canal at dusk + Pontocho dinner
why_worth_it: The canal, willows and lantern-lit machiya at dusk is the most romantic 30 minutes in Japan and takes no effort at all.
food_drink_pick: Kaiseki or obanzai on a Kamo-gawa yuka terrace (summer only)
best_time: The yuka riverside dining platforms are erected roughly May–September. If you're there in that window, book one.

specific_attraction: Fushimi Inari at 06:30, full ridge loop
why_worth_it: Sunrise turns a queue into a private mountain walk. This is the highest-leverage early alarm of the entire trip.
food_drink_pick: Breakfast back in town after
best_time: Take a taxi at 06:00. ¥2,000 buys you the version of Fushimi Inari worth having.

specific_attraction: Private tea ceremony + wagashi making, then Kiyomizu in late afternoon
why_worth_it: A hands-on 90-minute tea ceremony with a real practitioner beats a third temple by a mile, and you both come away having made something.
food_drink_pick: Matcha + namagashi you made yourself; Ippodo tea shop
best_time: This is the partner-version substitution principle in one line: cut a redundant temple, add a shared experience.

specific_attraction: Sagano Romantic Train + Hozugawa river boat, then Okochi Sanso
why_worth_it: The train-and-boat pairing is the best half-day in Kyoto and it's a shared, seated, scenic experience rather than a march.
food_drink_pick: Yudofu (hot-spring tofu) lunch by the river
best_time: Torokko closed roughly late Dec–Feb; book ahead in autumn. Kinkaku-ji is CUT — it's a one-way conveyor with no room to linger.

specific_attraction: Todai-ji + Nara Park deer, half day only
why_worth_it: Half a day gets you the Great Buddha and the deer. A full day gets you a second temple you'll forget.
food_drink_pick: Nakatanidou mochi pounding
best_time: Kasuga Taisha CUT unless the lantern festival is running.

specific_attraction: Dotonbori + a proper Osaka food crawl
why_worth_it: Osaka is the eating city. One night, done properly, is worth more than two days of sightseeing here.
food_drink_pick: Takoyaki, okonomiyaki, kushikatsu, then a Namba jazz kissa or highball bar
best_time: Shinsekai and USJ both CUT. Osaka earns exactly one great night in this version.

specific_attraction: Seven-bath onsen town walk in yukata + geta
why_worth_it: The whole town functions as one ryokan: you wander between seven public baths in yukata and wooden geta, willow trees over the canal. Nothing else in Japan feels like it.
food_drink_pick: Tajima beef; snow crab in winter (Nov–Mar) — one of Japan's great seasonal foods
best_time: Crab season roughly Nov 6–Mar. Kinosaki replaces the entire Amanohashidate/Nishi-Maizuru/Shikoku leg in this version — see the redundancy log.

specific_attraction: Peace Memorial Museum + Peace Park
why_worth_it: Non-negotiable, and better absorbed together with time to talk about it afterwards.
food_drink_pick: Hiroshima okonomiyaki
best_time: Don't stack anything cheerful immediately after. Leave the evening open.

specific_attraction: Stay overnight on the island — torii after the day-trippers leave
why_worth_it: After the last ferries, the island empties and the lit torii is essentially yours. Almost nobody does this and it's the best-value upgrade on the whole trip.
food_drink_pick: Grilled oysters, anago-meshi (conger eel rice), momiji manju
best_time: Check the tide table — high tide for the floating shot, low tide to walk to the base. Deer here will eat paper; keep tickets in a bag.

specific_attraction: Benesse Art Site: Chichu Art Museum, Lee Ufan, Yayoi Kusama pumpkins
why_worth_it: Tadao Ando's buried concrete museums holding four Monet water lilies in natural light. An island engineered as a single artwork.
food_drink_pick: Setouchi seafood; Sanuki udon on the mainland
best_time: Chichu requires timed advance tickets. Many museums close Mondays. Ferries are infrequent — build the day around the ferry timetable, not the reverse.

specific_attraction: Buffer day: last shopping, depachika food hall, airport
why_worth_it: A real buffer day means a cancelled ferry doesn't cost you the flight, and depachika basement food halls are the best souvenir shopping in Japan.
food_drink_pick: Depachika bento for the flight; Kyoto matcha and sake to take home
best_time: The solo version has no buffer day. The partner version always should.

specific_attraction: Kinrin Lake at dawn + luxury ryokan with private rotenburo
why_worth_it: Yufuin's top ryokan are among Japan's best and the mountain setting is gentler than Hakone's.
food_drink_pick: Bungo beef; Yufuin Milch cheesecake
best_time: Dawn mist Nov–Feb. Beppu's hells reduced to Umi Jigoku only — the 7-hell ticket is redundant.

specific_attraction: Sand bath at Beppu Kaihin Sunayu + jigoku-mushi steam cooking
why_worth_it: Two genuinely unusual shared experiences that aren't 'another hot spring'.
food_drink_pick: Steam-cooked seafood you load into the vent yourself
best_time: These are the two Beppu things that survive the redundancy cut.

transport: JR Yufuin no Mori scenic LtdExp
specific_attraction: Yufuin no Mori scenic train + Nakasu yatai + Dazaifu
why_worth_it: The Yufuin no Mori is a green-and-gold vintage-styled tourist train with a lounge car — the journey is the attraction.
food_drink_pick: Hakata tonkotsu; mentaiko; umegae-mochi at Dazaifu
best_time: Yufuin no Mori reserved seats sell out; book at a JR ticket office as soon as you land.

specific_attraction: Farm Tomita lavender fields + Blue Pond + Patchwork Road drive
why_worth_it: Rolling hills, lavender rows and a cobalt-blue pond. It looks like Provence relocated to Japan and it's a rental-car day, not a train day.
food_drink_pick: Furano melon; Biei soft-serve; Sapporo soup curry
best_time: Lavender peaks early-to-mid July ONLY. Outside that window this leg should be replaced with Otaru + Noboribetsu.

specific_attraction: Otaru canal evening + LeTAO + sushi street
why_worth_it: Gas lamps on the canal at night, and the best-value high-grade sushi in Japan.
food_drink_pick: Otaru sushi omakase; LeTAO double fromage
best_time: Sapporo city itself is CUT to a half-day — it's a modern grid city and Otaru does the atmosphere better.

specific_attraction: Tokyo DisneySea
why_worth_it: The one theme park that's worth it as a couple — DisneySea's design quality is on another level and Fantasy Springs is new.
best_time: Weekday dates only if you can help it. Book Premier Access for Fantasy Springs.

specific_attraction: Omakase sushi finale + Ginza / Ryogoku sumo if in season
why_worth_it: End on the single best meal of the trip rather than on a landmark.
food_drink_pick: High-end omakase — book 1–3 months ahead through the hotel concierge
best_time: Tokyo sumo basho: January, May, September.

specific_attraction: Gyeongbokgung + hanbok rental (free palace entry), Bukchon Hanok Village, Gwangjang Market, Hongdae nightlife, Namsan Tower
why_worth_it: Wearing hanbok gets you into the palaces free — a rare case where the touristy thing is also the economical one.
food_drink_pick: Gwangjang bindaetteok and mayak gimbap; Korean BBQ; a late-night chimaek (chicken + beer)
best_time: Bukchon has enforced quiet hours and photography restrictions on residential lanes after resident complaints — read the posted signs.

specific_attraction: DMZ tour: Imjingak, 3rd Infiltration Tunnel, Dora Observatory (JSA if operating)
why_worth_it: The most politically charged border on earth, and the observation platforms let you look directly into North Korea.
best_time: JSA/Panmunjom access is frequently suspended and separate from the standard DMZ tour. Passport details required days in advance; dress code enforced. VERIFY availability when booking.

specific_attraction: Jeonju Hanok Village and bibimbap; Gyeongju's Silla burial mounds, Bulguksa, Seokguram, Donggung Palace at night
